samples.summary: Default start affinity changed from backward to forward — a documented deviation from the issue's wording
samples.evidence: buildRects now defaults `startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'`. docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:18-26 records the issue said "keep the backward default" and that this PR deliberately deviates. The reasoning (a backward start on a boundary yields a zero-width rect) is sound and is now written into docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md, so this is a scope/spec-wording deviation rather than a defect — but it is a behavior change to affinity-less selections everywhere, including peer selections published by older clients.

samples.summary: Caret affinity round-trip added in editor.ts only works for click-produced positions; keyboard caret moves never put lineAffinity on the position object
samples.evidence: `Cursor.moveTo(pos, affinity)` (packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:28) stores the affinity in a separate `Cursor.lineAffinity` field and does not copy it onto `this.position`. Keyboard paths call `moveTo(newPos, 'forward'|hAffinity)` with a `newPos` that has no `lineAffinity` property (text-editor.ts:2780, 2795, 2818, 2831). Presence publishes `cursor.position` (editor.ts:1160/2069 -> fireCursorMoveCallbacks -> docs-view.tsx:399 -> updateCursorPos), so the new `restoreLocalCursor` affinity plumbing (editor.ts:3592) and the new integration test only exercise the click path; a Home-key caret at a wrap boundary still re-collapses onto the previous visual line after a remote change. Two sources of truth (Cursor.lineAffinity vs DocPosition.lineAffinity) are introduced without reconciliation in moveTo.

samples.summary: handleEnd's shift branch left without an explicit affinity while handleHome got one — asymmetric treatment of an equally ambiguous boundary
samples.evidence: handleHome now sets `focus: { ...newPos, lineAffinity: 'forward' }` (text-editor.ts:2811-2814), but handleEnd (2827) still sets `focus: newPos` with no affinity, and `cursor.moveTo(newPos)` uses the default. A visual line end is the same wrap-boundary offset; it only works out because the end default is 'backward', and it breaks the intent as soon as that endpoint becomes the range start (shift+End from a later anchor).

samples.summary: `anchorDocPosition`'s `lineAffinity` parameter is now redundant with `pos.lineAffinity` at every call site
samples.evidence: After the change, all three callers pass exactly `pos.lineAffinity` (lines 1000, 1003, 2999) or nothing (1209). The affinity now lives on the DocPosition itself, so the extra parameter is a second way to say the same thing and can silently diverge from the field it shadows.

samples.summary: restoreLocalCursor passes the affinity twice — once spread onto the position object and once as the moveTo argument
samples.evidence: The conditional spread `...(cursorPos.lineAffinity ? { lineAffinity } : {})` plus the second `cursorPos.lineAffinity` argument encode the same value in two places; only the argument is read by Cursor.moveTo (cursor.ts:28-30), the property is carried for republishing. Worth a single helper or a moveTo that reads pos.lineAffinity.

samples.summary: Design doc pins a hard-coded source line number (`editor.ts:1563`) that nothing checks
samples.evidence: The prose says peer caret rendering hard-codes backward "(`editor.ts:1563`)". Nested design docs are not link/ref-checked by CI, and the reference goes stale on the next edit to editor.ts; naming the function/symbol would survive.

finding.summary: docs-presence.md contradicts the code this same delta ships: the `DocsPresence` snippet still types `activeCursorPos` as `{ blockId, offset }`, and the §4 prose added in this delta asserts "`activeCursorPos` is not typed for the field" — but the delta adds `lineAffinity?: 'forward' | 'backward'` to `activeCursorPos` in `packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:25`. The canonical presence design doc is the wire-shape record for Docs presence (CONTRIBUTING requires the data-model change be folded into the canonical subsystem doc), so it must show the field on the caret payload too, or the field should not be added. As written, the doc will mislead the next reader about what the caret presence payload carries.
finding.evidence: docs-presence.md snippet: `activeCursorPos?: { blockId: string; offset: number; }` and prose "The peer *caret* still resolves `'backward'`: `activeCursorPos` is not typed for the field" vs users.ts adding `lineAffinity?: 'forward' | 'backward'` to activeCursorPos.

verdict.reason: The claimed contradiction does not exist in this repository. The `DocsPresence` snippet in the canonical design doc already types the field on the caret payload: `docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:88-92` shows `activeCursorPos?: { blockId: string; offset: number; lineAffinity?: 'forward' | 'backward' }`, which matches `packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:21-28` field-for-field (including the `activeSelection` anchor/focus affinity at doc lines 95-96 vs users.ts:33-34). The prose the finding quotes is also misquoted: `docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:191-197` says "The peer *caret* still resolves `'backward'`: the field rides along on `activeCursorPos`, but peer caret rendering hard-codes the backward reading" — i.e. it explicitly states the field IS on the payload and only the renderer ignores it. A repo-wide grep for the asserted phrase "not typed for the field" returns zero matches. Doc line 387-389 likewise distinguishes the caret's `'backward'` default from selection endpoints carrying their own affinity, so the doc is coherent with the shipped wire shape and would not mislead the next reader.
